reason: While Moses expresses self-doubt and acknowledges his limitations ('I am not a man of words... slow of speech and slow of tongue'), this passage does not present such humility as a model of good leadership. Instead, God's response is marked by anger ('the anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses'), indicating displeasure with Moses' objections and reluctance. The passage emphasizes divine will overcoming human doubt and resistance, rather than affirming that humility in facing one's perceived inadequacy is a leadership ideal. God overrides Moses' objections rather than endorsing his self-aware reluctance as exemplary leadership conduct.
